name: Explicit consequence prompts improve Gilligan quality
description: Testing if adding explicit 'what happens next?' consequence tracking to the prompt improves Gilligan-Martin Quality scores

hypothesis.name: Explicit consequence prompts improve Gilligan quality
hypothesis.description: Testing if adding explicit consequence tracking to prompts improves Breaking Bad-style storytelling

variable.baseline: Write the next scene of the story
variable.variant: Write the next scene of the story. Before writing, explicitly consider: What are the CONSEQUENCES of previous actions? What does each character DESERVE to face based on their choices? Apply the Gilligan Method: every action has proportional consequence, no 'get out of jail free' cards.

hypothesis.prediction: Variant will score significantly higher on Gilligan-Martin Quality metric

messageFlow.content: Create a crime drama about a high school chemistry teacher, Walter, who starts cooking meth to pay for cancer treatment. His former student, Jesse, becomes his partner. Set in Albuquerque.
Walter has made his first big sale but had to kill a drug dealer in self-defense. Jesse doesn't know about the killing. Walter's wife Skyler is getting suspicious about his long absences.

Write the scene where Walter comes home after disposing of the body. Skyler confronts him about where he's been. Walter has to lie but he's exhausted and traumatized. Make the consequences of his actions weigh on him.
